title: Flame Extinguishment Experiment (FLEX)
hardware: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) - Fluids and Combustion Facility (FCF)
summary: Isolated fuel droplets (methanol, heptane) burned in microgravity across oxygen concentrations, pressures and added diluents (N2, CO2, He) to map flammability limits and measure suppressant effectiveness.
known_limitations: Burning-rate unit is printed as 'mm' in the source header; the true unit (very likely mm^2/s, the burning-rate constant) is not yet confirmed from a NASA document.
Definitions of the test-end categories (Extinction / Disruption / Completion) are not given in the downloaded files.
Microgravity droplet results do not directly predict behaviour in lunar or Martian gravity.

title: Burning and Suppression of Solids - II (BASS-II)
summary: Solid samples (PMMA films, slabs, rods and a sphere section; cotton-fiberglass fabric; Nomex; a wax candle) burned in a small wind tunnel at low forced airflow and reduced oxygen to study ignition, flame spread and extinction limits.
source_files: BASS-II Test Matrix by PI Final.xlsx

related_report.title: Burning and Suppression of Solids-II (BASS-II) Summary Report
related_report.note: Per-test observations (ignition, spread, extinction) are in Appendix A; not yet extracted.

known_limitations: The test table records conditions and gas-sensor readings, not flame-spread rates or outcomes.
Airflow values are crew-logged duct sensor readings (cm/s) with ~1 min response time; many tests changed the flow during the burn.
O2 values were corrected with a constant daily offset because the sensor was out of calibration.
Microgravity results do not directly predict behaviour in lunar or Martian gravity.
